title: Preserve message-stack native-scroll ownership across lifecycle boundaries
outcome: The shared native-scroll ownership lease can be erased before its landing scroll frame: virtualized-conversation-scroll-events effect cleanup clears it during ordinary dependency-driven re-registration, and markUserScroll clears it before deciding whether the next no-op boundary tick should claim a replacement. A scrollbar drag rerender or a fast downward wheel burst can therefore lose pointer/wheel attribution and fail to reattach at physical bottom. Keep the lease across ordinary effect reruns and no-op same-burst input, clear it only on true node detach/unmount or a superseding owner/direction, and cover lifecycle-separated mousedown/rerender/scroll plus two wheel ticks before the first native scroll.
acceptance: Ownership survives effect re-registration and same-burst no-op ticks; true detach, blur/cancel, expiry, opposite direction, or a superseding owner clears it; lifecycle-separated scrollbar and multi-tick wheel regressions pass.
